description:
Artturi Lehkonen etched his name into Stanley Cup history with the championship-winning goal in Game 6 of the 2022 Final. With the game tied 1-1 midway through the second period, Lehkonen found himself in the right place at the right time. Nathan MacKinnon’s attempted pass deflected off a defender and landed on Lehkonen’s stick. Wasting no time, he fired a quick shot past Andrei Vasilevskiy at 12:28, giving the Avalanche a 2-1 lead they wouldn’t relinquish.  
Lehkonen’s opportunistic goal sealed Colorado’s first Stanley Cup in over two decades, capping off a playoff run where his clutch play and tireless effort were key to the Avalanche’s success. On a roster loaded with talent, Lehkonen’s ability to seize the moment ensured his place in Avs lore.

description:
Sam Bennett, who led all players with 15 playoff goals, set a new NHL record with 13 road goals in a single postseason. A cornerstone of Florida’s second consecutive Stanley Cup championship, Bennett’s remarkable performances earned him the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP. 
In the First Round against Tampa Bay, Bennett delivered the decisive blow, breaking a tie late in the second period with a goal that stood as the series-clincher. In the Second Round against Toronto, with the Panthers clinging to a 1-0 lead late in the third period of Game 4, Bennett struck again. Capitalizing on a loose puck in the neutral zone, he charged toward the net, faked a shot, outwaited the goalie, and fired it home, effectively sealing the game and tying the series. 
Bennett’s final goal in this highlight epitomized the grit and tenacity of Panthers hockey. In the second period of Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final, Bennett delivered two thunderous hits in the defensive zone, fought to clear the puck, and capped the shift with a breakaway snipe to extend Florida’s lead.

description:
After retiring in 1971 following a legendary 25-season career with the Detroit Red Wings, Gordie Howe was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 1972. However, in 1973, at the age of 45, Howe came out of retirement to join his sons, Mark and Marty, in the World Hockey Association (WHA). The trio played six seasons together in the WHA before playing one final season in the NHL during the 1979-80 campaign, which marked the last year in the league for "Mr. Hockey."  
Gordie was chosen to participate in the 1980 NHL All-Star Game, held in the heart of Detroit, Michigan. At that time, he was donning the colors of the Hartford Whalers, but as he stepped onto the ice in the city that had embraced him throughout his legendary career, the atmosphere became electric. The crowd erupted in a powerful, emotional standing ovation that lasted over five minutes, a profound testament to the love and admiration they held for him. In that moment, it was not just a tribute; it was a celebration of a hockey icon whose impact on the game and the community would be cherished forever.  In that game, Howe earned an assist setting up Real Cloutier for a goal late in the third period, contributing to the Wales Conference All-Stars' 6-3 victory.  
Over 26 NHL seasons, Howe scored 801 goals and 1,049 assists in 1,767 games. When including his WHA career, he totaled 975 goals and 2,358 points over 32 professional seasons. A 23-time NHL All-Star, Howe won six Hart Trophies and four Stanley Cups, and remarkably, finished in the top five in NHL scoring for 20 consecutive seasons.

description:
In the Stanley Cup Playoffs, teams sometimes need their goaltender to “steal” a game to stay alive. In Game 6 of the 2001 Stanley Cup Final, Patrick Roy delivered a masterclass on the road to force a decisive Game 7. Roy was spectacular, especially in the first period, turning aside multiple Grade-A chances to keep the game scoreless. His heroics gave Colorado the chance to find their stride, leading to a 4-0 victory and a clutch shutout for Roy. Two nights later in Game 7, Roy was once again brilliant. He stopped 25 of 26 shots, including a critical pad save early in the first period to preserve a one-goal lead — an advantage the Avalanche would never surrender. During the 2001 playoffs, Roy posted an exceptional 16-7 record, a .934 save percentage, a 1.70 goals-against average, and four shutouts. For his dominance and leadership, Roy earned his third Conn Smythe Trophy, more than any player in NHL history. The victory also marked his fourth and final Stanley Cup championship, capping off a legendary career that includes three Vezina Trophies and an indelible legacy as one of the greatest goaltenders of all time.

description:
Nominated as a finalist for the Calder Trophy as the League's best rookie, Macklin Celebrini had an outstanding first year with the San Jose Sharks. The 2024 first overall pick showcased the incredible skill set that made him the top choice the previous summer.  
One of his standout moments came in Vancouver, where he unleashed a laser-like shot with pinpoint accuracy, going bar down on the short side and beating the goalie’s glove for his 25th goal of the season—his final tally. Celebrini finished the year with 63 points, tied for second among rookies despite playing fewer games. His impressive 0.90 points per game led all rookies with more than a handful of games played, further cementing his place as one of the most exciting young talents in the League.

description:
Lane Hutson claimed the Calder Trophy as the NHL's top rookie for the 2024-25 season, tying Larry Murphy’s record for most assists by a rookie defenseman (60 in 1980-81). He also became the first blueliner to surpass 60 points as a rookie since Nicklas Lidstrom (60 in 1991-92) and matched Phil Housley (66 in 1982-83) for fourth-most points by a rookie defenseman in NHL history. Hutson’s dynamic skating and playmaking produced countless highlights throughout his debut season. In one memorable moment, he netted his first NHL goal by beating Winnipeg netminder Connor Hellebuyck (winner of the Hart Trophy, Vezina Trophy and William M. Jennings Trophy in 2024-25). Later, in a critical playoff push, Hutson delivered a pinpoint cross-ice pass to Nick Suzuki for the game-winning goal against the defending Stanley Cup champions. Near season’s end, with playoff hopes on the line, Hutson scored a jaw-dropping go-ahead goal against Philadelphia. Starting behind his own net, he weaved through defenders coast-to-coast before roofing a sharp-angle shot top shelf—a fitting exclamation point on an incredible rookie campaign.

description:
On April 15, 2024, Lucas Raymond delivered a clutch performance to keep the Red Wings' playoff hopes alive with a dramatic late-game goal in Detroit. Trailing 4–3 with under two minutes remaining in the third period, defenseman Shayne Gostisbehere made a key play by leaping to keep the puck inside the blue line, keeping the Red Wings’ attack alive. Raymond seized the moment, taking a pass from David Perron and firing a quick shot past Canadiens goaltender Sam Montembeault to tie the game with just 1:17 left on the clock.   Raymond would later step up again in overtime, scoring the game-winner.  
While the Red Wings ultimately missed the playoffs, Lucas Raymond’s late-game heroics were a bright spot in the final stretch of the season. His ability to deliver in high-pressure moments highlighted his poise and skill, marking a memorable night for the young star as he continued to show why he’s one of the brightest talents in Detroit’s future.

description:
In January 2006, during his rookie season, Alex Ovechkin scored a remarkable goal that has since become iconic among hockey fans worldwide. Playing against the Phoenix Coyotes, with Wayne Gretzky as their head coach, Ovechkin pulled off a stunning feat by scoring while on his back. Ovechkin capped off his rookie season in spectacular fashion, finishing with 52 goals, 106 points, and winning the Calder Trophy.

description:
A three-time Art Ross Trophy winner, Nikita Kucherov has been a dominant force in the NHL for more than a decade. Renowned as a world-class playmaker, Kucherov ranks third in assists since entering the League. But he's more than just a passer—Kucherov’s dual-threat capability shines through with three seasons of 40+ goals to his name. 
In the first sequence, Kucherov showcases his coast-to-coast brilliance against the Avalanche, weaving through defenders before setting up Jake Guentzel for a short-side tap-in goal. Then, on a Lightning power play, he demonstrates his creativity with a fake shot-pass, threading the puck through traffic to find Brayden Point on the far side for a perfect tape-to-tape connection. Finally, Kucherov’s scoring prowess takes center stage as he streaks down the wing, eluding a defender, and snipes a shot off the crossbar before calmly following up to tap in his own rebound. 
The 2024-25 season further highlighted Kucherov’s brilliance as he led the league in points for the second straight year, solidifying his place among the NHL’s elite.

description:
Wyatt Johnston delivered a clutch performance for the Dallas Stars in Game 3 of the First Round of the 2024 Stanley Cup Playoffs, scoring the overtime winner to secure a 3-2 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights. With the series hanging in the balance and Dallas facing the threat of an 0-3 hole, Johnston stepped up late in overtime. Skating down the wing, he froze Logan Thompson with a quick move before roofing a sharp-angle shot into the top corner, sparking wild celebrations and ending a six-game losing streak against the defending champs.  
Johnston had already given the Stars an early lead, scoring in the first period, and finished the game with two goals and eight shots. His overtime heroics not only cut the series deficit to 2-1 but proved to be a turning point. Dallas went on to win the series in seven games, with Johnston’s big moment helping to reignite the team’s playoff run and solidifying the 20-year-old as one of the rising stars in the league.

description:
Playing in his home country of Finland during the 2022 NHL Global Series, Mikko Rantanen thrilled the fans by scoring a hat trick. His first goal showcased his skill and patience as he maneuvered to the far side of the net, firing the puck from a sharp angle into the back of the goal. He capped off the night by scoring an empty-netter for his third goal, part of a 55-goal campaign during the 2022-23 season, marking the first time in his career that he reached the 50-goal milestone.

description:
Mario Lemieux’s NHL rookie season in 1984-85 was nothing short of legendary. The Pittsburgh Penguins’ first overall draft pick wasted no time making his mark, scoring on his very first shift in the NHL—a harbinger of the greatness to come. Lemieux finished his rookie campaign with 100 points (43 goals, 57 assists) in 73 games, earning the Calder Memorial Trophy as the league’s top rookie.  
Lemieux made an unforgettable impression at the 1985 NHL All-Star Game as well.  The 19-year-old phenom tallied two goals and one assist, earning MVP honors. Lemieux’s commanding performance on the league’s biggest stage showcased his incredible skill and composure, cementing his status as one of hockey’s brightest young stars.  
Displaying a combination of size, skill, and hockey IQ rarely seen in the sport, Lemieux dazzled fans with his smooth skating, pinpoint passing, and deadly scoring touch. His electrifying play quickly established him as a transformative player and laid the foundation for one of the most storied careers in hockey history, solidifying his status as a once-in-a-generation talent right from the start.

description:
Charging down the middle of the ice, defenseman Borje Salming took a pass that sent him on a breakaway. Alone against the goalie, Salming snapped a shot glove-side, finding the back of the net during the 1976 Stanley Cup Playoffs.   
Later in his career, in a matchup against New Jersey, Salming took a pass in stride and snapped a quick shot past the Devils goaltender, bringing the Toronto crowd to its feet.  
A stalwart for the Toronto Maple Leafs for 16 of his 17 NHL seasons, Salming was a trailblazer for European players, establishing himself as a star in the league. In 1996, he became the first European-born and trained player inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame, cementing his enduring legacy.

description:
On March 26, 2022, before a game against the New Jersey Devils, Nicklas Backstrom was honored for reaching the 1,000-point milestone earlier that season. The evening began with a heartfelt pregame ceremony, where Backstrom received tributes from teammates, coaches, and fellow NHL stars, recognizing his career achievement. 
In the game itself, Backstrom delivered a memorable performance, scoring the key go-ahead goal in the third period to break a 2-2 tie and help the Capitals secure a 4-3 victory. As the crowd roared in approval, fans celebrated the moment by showering the ice with thousands of foam apples, a fitting tribute to Backstrom’s legendary playmaking ability.

description:
The Florida Panthers entered overtime of Game 3 against the Toronto Maple Leafs with the possibility of falling behind 3-0 in their Second Round series. In that high-pressure moment, late-season acquisition Brad Marchand delivered a crucial goal, adding yet another highlight to his storied career. 

Marchand’s shot toward the net took a fortuitous deflection, redirecting past the goaltender and securing the pivotal overtime victory for Florida in a game that felt like a must-win. The Panthers rode the momentum from that critical goal to eventually win the series in seven games. Marchand’s standout performance in the Second Round included a League-leading eight points and an impressive +6 rating, solidifying his impact on the Panthers' postseason success.

description:
In his first-ever NHL game in Chicago, Connor Bedard thrilled the home crowd by scoring his first goal on United Center ice against the Vegas Golden Knights. Early in the first period, the 18-year-old phenom found himself alone in front of the net, burying a quick wrist shot past the goaltender. Bedard, who went on to win the Calder Trophy as the league’s top rookie, capped his debut season with an impressive 22 goals in just 68 games, cementing his place as one of the game's brightest young stars.
